extracted.intended_audience: general readers and cruise passengers interested in the Costa Concordia disaster and maritime safety
extracted.subtask_description: A factual blog-style summary of the Costa Concordia sinking focused on the captain's actions, the legal findings and sentences, crew convictions, and subsequent safety changes in cruising. Useful for readers wanting an overview of responsibility, criminal charges, and procedural lessons from the incident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Captain responsibility for safety and navigation
rubrics_metrics.description: "Schettino ... was responsible for overseeing all safety aspects of the ship and cruise, including setting the course for the ship to follow."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The captain is expected to set and follow a safe, approved course and oversee all onboard safety. The article describes that Schettino chose to sail closer to the coast than usual, raising questions about adherence to his duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to approved route / avoidance of unauthorized sail-pasts
rubrics_metrics.description: Costa Cruises say that he didn’t take the approved route; Schettino said Costa had asked him to perform a sail past.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deviation from an approved route or performing an unapproved 'sail past' is treated as a procedural breach and is scrutinized as a possible cause of accidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep navigational alarm systems active
rubrics_metrics.description: Schettino said that before approaching this area, he had turned off the alarm system for the navigational systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disabling navigation alarms is an unsafe anti-pattern; alarms provide critical alerts (e.g., proximity to reefs) and turning them off can contribute to collisions and is considered negligent behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain situational awareness and avoid risky close-coast maneuvers
rubrics_metrics.description: When Schettino saw waves breaking on the reef, he turned abruptly and swung the side of the ship onto the reef. It’s reported he sailed closer to the coast than usual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sailing too close to shore and abrupt corrective maneuvers that put the vessel at risk are examples of imprudence and negligence cited by investigators and courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid onboard distractions and unauthorized personal guests / avoid substance impairment
rubrics_metrics.description: Another theory is that Schettino was distracted by a lady he had brought onboard the ship... Some accounts have reported that Schettino’s hair showed trace amounts of cocaine and that there was a considerable amount of cocaine on the ship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bringing unauthorized companions into operational areas, personal distractions, or substance use are presented as potential causal factors that undermine proper command performance and constitute negligent or unprofessional conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate and accurate emergency communication (mayday) to authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The ship hit the reef at 10.12 pm, and authorities were not alerted to the problem until 10.42pm — despite port officials asking the Costa Concordia if there was a problem on board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to promptly declare distress (mayday) or to accurately report the situation to port/authorities is a procedural lapse that exacerbates harm and is examined in legal proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to coordinate evacuation and ensure passengers are evacuated before abandoning ship
rubrics_metrics.description: It’s a maritime tradition that the Captain always goes down with his ship. The Captain should make sure that everybody else is off the ship before they disembark. Costa Concordia’s Captain didn’t do this — he decided instead to save himself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The captain must coordinate evacuation (e.g., go to the bow, climb up the emergency ladder, tell how many people remain) and must not abandon ship while passengers remain onboard. Abandoning ship while passengers are still aboard is cited as a core basis for criminal charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obey orders from Coastguard and other authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: "He disobeyed orders from the Coastguard to go back to the ship." — exchange quoted from Coastguard official Gregorio de Falco.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance with direct orders from rescue authorities during an emergency is a required procedural duty; disobeying such orders is treated as dereliction and can inform criminal culpability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal liability standards applied (manslaughter, causing shipwreck, abandoning ship)
rubrics_metrics.description: Captain Schettino was detained on suspicion of manslaughter. He was charged with causing a shipwreck caused by ‘imprudence, negligence and incompetence’. He was also charged with abandoning 300 people who were unable to disembark the ship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts evaluate whether actions meet criminal offense elements (e.g., manslaughter, shipwreck caused by negligence, abandonment). The article lists the specific charges and the 2016 sentence breakdown (10 years for multiple manslaughters, 5 years for causing a shipwreck, 1 year for abandoning passengers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Crew accountability and specific misconduct categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Several crew members were convicted for offenses including abandoning a ship, delaying an adequate response, directing the ship in the wrong direction, and manslaughter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The captain is not the only accountable party; crew members can be charged for failing to respond properly, giving wrong directions, delaying rescue efforts or abandoning ship. The article provides names and prison times as examples of how accountability was applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for onboard safety drills (muster drills) and changes after the accident
rubrics_metrics.description: At the time of the sinking, guests boarding a cruise had to have a safety drill within 24 hours of embarkation, this meant that guests who had embarked on the day of the accident hadn’t yet had their safety drill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-accident safety policy changes targeted muster drills timing and procedures to ensure passengers receive safety briefings before departure or earlier during embarkation to improve emergency readiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensuring sufficient lifesaving equipment (lifeboats) and ongoing safety improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Many people worry that cruise ships don’t have enough lifeboats if an emergency evacuation is needed. Rest assured, they do. ... Find out about the safety improvements made onboard cruise ships after the fire onboard the Star Princess in 2006 here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators must provide adequate lifeboats and continually implement safety improvements informed by prior incidents; the article references past incidents and safety upgrades as part of evaluating safety preparedness.
